transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you lately that made you decide to come here today?

Yeah, I guess what pushed me to come in is… I kind of went from just being one of the regular crew guys, you know, mowing and planting and doing what I’m told, to suddenly trying to run like three different bids at once. I was calling city people, trying to line up plant suppliers, messaging everybody I knew about this park idea I had—like coworkers, old friends, people I barely talk to.

And it just… it wouldn’t shut off. I mean, I like landscaping, I’ve always liked making places look better, and there’s this one park near where I grew up that’s always bothered me because the beds are all wrecked and nobody waters anything right—but this got way bigger than that. I couldn’t leave it alone. That’s what made me think maybe I needed to talk to someone.
Can you tell me if you’ve felt unusually energized, had racing thoughts, or felt like you didn’t need much sleep during this time?

Yeah… I mean, I was definitely going more than normal. I’d be up before daylight loading tools into the truck, then I’d start sketching out beds or checking prices on native plants before work even started. And then after being outside all day—like, after a full day of hauling, digging, all that—I still felt like I had to keep going.

It’s weird because usually after work I’m wiped, you know? Like my uncle used to say landscaping either makes you sleep good or hate your knees by thirty, and I’m kind of already there. But during that stretch I’d get home and still be thinking about plant lists and layouts and who I needed to call next. It just felt like there was more to do and I couldn’t really put it down.

During that time when you were so full of energy and couldn’t slow down, did you feel unusually high, extremely confident, or maybe even irritable — like you were on top of the world or couldn’t be stopped?

Yeah… yeah, I did. Not like happy exactly, more like I was fired up, like I could see the whole thing and everybody else was moving too slow. I felt… bigger than myself, I guess.

And then if one of the guys was like, “Man, maybe don’t call them again,” or “That plan’s too much,” I’d get pissed fast. Like way more than it deserved. I snapped at a coworker over something small, and then later I was thinking, why did I come at him like that? But in the moment it felt like they were just in my way.
